title: Rollback UX wire notes (Optimize config safe-apply + rollback)
linked_artifacts: Jira: SUP-2431 (rollback button missing for Dedicated)
content:
Purpose
Working notes for Console UX for Optimize config version history / compare / safe-apply / rollback. This is intentionally rough: wireframe-by-words, copy drafts, and decision log. Audience: Product + Console engineering.

Scope reminder (what the UI must support)
- Operators need to see immutable version history by scope (customer, deployment mode, region/cluster, route, model).
- Safe-apply wizard: preflight validation + preview diff + optional canary + metric gates.
- One-click rollback: to any prior known-good version, with clear blast radius + guardrails.
- Auditability: show who/when/why + links to audit log events and correlation/request IDs.
- Permissions: apply and rollback are separate privileges.

Primary personas (in order of “we can’t break this”)
1) On-call / SRE (Rafael/Sean’s world)
- Often stressed, limited context, needs fast path.
- Wants obvious status, fast rollback button, and “did it work?” checklist.

2) Platform operator (internal + enterprise operator)
- Wants controlled rollout (canary) and clear diff.
- Needs to understand guardrails and how to override.

3) Customer admin (Dedicated/Private)
- Expects change management patterns: approvals, audit trails, and minimal ambiguity.
- May not have deep system knowledge; copy needs to be less Redwood-internal.

Information architecture (draft)
Left nav: Optimize > Configs
Subtabs:
A) Current (live view)
B) History (timeline)
C) Safe apply (wizard; can also be launched from Current)
D) Audit log (filtered to this scope; optional, may live in global audit area)

Key decision: put Rollback entry points in TWO places
- In History tab: for “roll back to version X” mental model.
- In Current tab: “Rollback…” CTA in overflow menu next to “Apply new version” (faster for on-call).

Naming (still open)
- “Optimization config” vs “Optimize config” vs “Serving optimization config”
  Draft: UI label = “Optimization config” (avoid product-code name). In tooltips / docs mention it’s used by batching/caching/quantization/routing.


SCREEN 1: History (version timeline)
Goal: quick scan of changes, choose a version, compare, or rollback.

Layout notes
- Header: [Scope picker] + [Environment badge: Hosted/Dedicated/Private] + [Region/Cluster] + [Route] + [Model]
- Right side header: [Create new version] primary, [Safe apply] secondary (depending on entry point), kebab menu.
- Main: timeline table (newest first).

Timeline row fields (minimum viable)
- Version: v17 (click opens details drawer)
- Status badge: Live / Applied / Rolled back / Failed / Canary / Deprecated
- Created: timestamp (local) + relative time
- Author: name + auth method icon (Console/API)
- Reason: short text (optional but strongly encouraged)
- Ticket link: e.g., LINEAR-ENG-4824 / JIRA-SUP-2418
- Applied to: “us-east-prod / cluster-gpu-12” (collapsed, expandable)
- Actions: Compare, Rollback (if permitted), Copy JSON (advanced)

Row details drawer (right panel)
- Summary: Version, created, author, reason, links
- Applied status: live or not, and where
- Audit event links (deep link to event id)
- “Compare with…” dropdown (defaults to current live)
- CTA row: [Compare] [Rollback to this version]

Notes for “known-good”
- We need a user-visible signal for “known-good”. Engineering says we can infer from apply success + post-apply health check result (gates passed). This needs a badge.
  Draft badges:
  - “Known-good” (green, only if apply succeeded AND post-apply checks passed)
  - “Applied (no checks)” (gray, for earlier versions created pre-gating)
  - “Failed apply” (red)
  - “Rolled back” (purple) with link to rollback event


SCREEN 2: Compare (diff/preview)
Goal: show what will change, in a way that is legible for nested config.

Interaction
- Launch from History row: “Compare” (this version vs current live)
- Or from Safe apply step: auto-opens compare preview.

Structure proposal
- Two-column compare with a toggle:
  - Default: “Changed only” view (collapsed)
  - Toggle: “Full config” view (advanced)
- Provide three levels:
  1) Summary chips (high-level)
  2) Grouped sections (batching/caching/quantization/routing)
  3) Raw JSON diff (copyable) behind “Advanced” expander

Summary chips (draft)
- “Batching: max_batch_tokens 4096 → 6144”
- “KV cache: prefix_cache enabled → disabled”
- “Quantization: profile fp16 → int8”
- “Routing: fallback policy unchanged”

Section ordering (draft)
1) Safety/guardrails (if present)
2) Scheduling & batching
3) Cache
4) Quantization profile
5) Routing policy
6) Other / unknown fields (if any)

Diff rendering rules (proposal)
- Red/green inline for scalar changes.
- For lists/maps: show count change and allow expand to see items.
- Flag any “high-risk” fields with an icon and tooltip (based on validator severity):
  - Quantization profile changes
  - Disabling cache
  - Increasing max batch tokens beyond recommended threshold

Copy: Compare modal title (draft)
- “Compare versions”
- Subtitle: “Showing changes from v16 (Live) to v17 (Draft)”

Compare modal footer CTAs (contextual)
- If in History: [Close] [Rollback to vX] (if permitted)
- If in Safe apply: [Back] [Continue to validation]


SCREEN 3: Safe apply (wizard)
Goal: make change safe by default; guide users through validation and rollout.

Wizard steps (proposal)
Step 0 (optional): Choose base
- “Start from live config” (default)
- “Start from version…” (dropdown)

Step 1: Edit or import
- For MVP, do NOT build full form editor for all fields.
- Provide:
  - Text area JSON editor (with schema hints)
  - “Apply recommended changes” button (future; likely post-MVP)
  - Validate JSON syntax inline
- Callout: “You are creating a new immutable version. You can roll back at any time.”

Step 2: Preview diff
- Show Compare UI (changed-only default)
- Require a short “Reason for change” text field (see security requirements)
- Ticket link field (optional but recommended)

Step 3: Preflight validation
- Display results with severity:
  - Blocking (must fix)
  - Warning (can proceed with acknowledgement)
  - Info
- Each rule should show:
  - What failed
  - Why it matters
  - Suggested fix
  - Link to docs (eventually)

Validation results layout (draft)
- Top summary: “2 blocking, 3 warnings, 4 info”
- Expandable list with categories:
  - Schema & compatibility
  - Capacity / batching bounds
  - Runtime risk heuristics
  - Propagation simulation (dry run)

Step 4: Rollout strategy (canary)
- Toggle: “Use canary apply” (default ON for prod scopes; OFF for dev)
- If ON:
  - Canary size: 5% (dropdown 1/5/10/25)
  - Duration: 10 min default
  - Gates: p95 latency, error rate, saturation (read-only default thresholds; can request override if permission)
  - “What happens if gates fail?”: auto-halt + show rollback button (NOT auto-rollback, per non-goal)
- If OFF:
  - Show warning: “Applying without canary increases risk. Recommended only for low-traffic or emergency changes.”

Step 5: Apply
- Show “Applying…” progress with per-scope status (region/cluster)
- Provide correlation id + link to audit event stream
- Provide escape hatch: “Stop rollout” (if supported) or “Rollback” once apply completes but health is bad

Post-apply screen
- Status: “Applied successfully” vs “Applied, checks pending” vs “Failed”
- Checklist component:
  - Confirm error rate is stable
  - Confirm p95 latency stable
  - Confirm saturation stable
  - Confirm customer incident channel updated (optional)
- Buttons: [View in History] [Rollback] [Close]


SCREEN 4: One-click rollback
Goal: allow fast rollback with minimal mistakes and clear communication.

Entry points
- From History row: “Rollback to v15”
- From Live config page: “Rollback…” then choose target version
- From incident-bot link (deep link): should land on rollback confirmation with scope prefilled

Rollback confirmation modal (draft)
Title: “Rollback optimization config?”
Body copy (default, prod):
- “You’re about to roll back this scope to version v15 (known-good). This will replace the current live config (v17) across: [scope summary].”
- “Rollback is a whole-config rollback. Any changes made since v15 will be reverted.”
- “This action is logged and may affect customer traffic.”

Fields
- Target version selector (if entered from Live)
- Reason for rollback (required for enterprise tiers, optional internal?)
  Draft requirement: required whenever scope includes prod OR customer-owned tenant.
- Checkbox: “I understand this will revert the entire config” (only if diff includes high-risk fields)

Blast radius summary (must be obvious)
- Show as a boxed section near top:
  - Deployment: Hosted / Dedicated / Private
  - Customer: [name/id]
  - Regions/clusters: list count + “View details”
  - Routes/models affected: route + model (or “Multiple”)

Diff snippet inside rollback modal (proposal)
- Show top 3 changes between target and current live as bullets + “View full diff” link
- Example bullets:
  - “Quantization: int8 → fp16”
  - “Batching: max_batch_tokens 6144 → 4096”
  - “Prefix cache: disabled → enabled”

Modal footer buttons
- [Cancel]
- [Rollback] (primary, destructive style)
- If permission missing: replace Rollback with “Request access” (links to internal process / helpdesk)

Rollback progress page/state
- After confirming, show a dedicated progress view (avoid leaving user guessing):
  - “Rollback started” + correlation id
  - Per-region apply status (Pending / In progress / Succeeded / Failed)
  - “View audit log” link
  - “Notify incident channel” button (internal only; posts to incident-bot with link)

Rollback completion
- Success state: “Rolled back to v15”
- Provide “Validate recovery” checklist (same as post-apply)
- Provide “Re-apply v17” (secondary) ONLY if we’re confident we can treat it as a version (NOTE: might be confusing; potentially hide behind advanced).

Failure state (partial propagation)
- Copy must be calm and action-oriented.
  Draft:
  - “Rollback partially applied. Some clusters did not update.”
  - “Traffic may see inconsistent behavior until resolved.”
  - Show failed clusters + error messages + “Escalate to on-call runtime” link.
  - Offer: “Retry rollback” (idempotent) if safe.


Copy drafts (toasts/banners)
- Success toast (apply): “Applied version v17. Monitoring health checks…”
- Success toast (rollback): “Rolled back to v15. Monitoring health checks…”
- Blocking validation banner: “Fix blocking issues before you can apply.”
- Warning acknowledgement (checkbox label): “I understand the risks and want to proceed.”
- Permission banner (RBAC):
  - “You don’t have permission to roll back configs for this scope.”
  - Secondary: “Request access” (internal) / “Contact your org admin” (external)


Decision log (running)
1) Whole-config rollback (no partial rollback in v1)
- Decision: Yes (aligns with ADR; reduces foot-guns).
- UX implication: must say “replaces entire config” and show diff summary.
- Owner: Marissa / Dylan. Date: 2024-11-20.

2) Require “Reason” field
- Decision: Required for rollback in prod/customer scopes; required for apply when canary OFF in prod; optional in dev.
- Rationale: audit/compliance + post-incident review usefulness.
- Open question: Should we also require ticket link? (lean “recommended” not required).
- Owner: Fiona / Marcus input. Date: 2024-11-22.

3) Canary default
- Decision: Default ON for prod scopes. Default OFF for dev/sandbox.
- Rationale: safety by default; aligns SRE expectations.
- Owner: Paula / Neha. Date: 2024-11-25.

4) “Known-good” badge criteria
- Decision: Apply succeeded + gates passed OR explicit operator mark? Lean: automated.
- Risk: older versions won’t have gates; show “Applied (no checks)”.
- Owner: Logan / Allison. Date: 2024-11-27.

5) Show raw JSON
- Decision: Keep behind “Advanced”. Don’t force JSON on casual operators.
- Owner: Kenji. Date: 2024-11-28.

6) Rollback CTA placement
- Decision: Keep in History rows and in Current page overflow.
- Owner: Kenji/Marissa. Date: 2024-12-01.


Open questions / TODO
- Scope picker design: how to prevent users from thinking they’re rolling back “everything” when they are scoped to a route/model. Need a strong breadcrumb of scope.
- Dedicated vs Private: do we display cluster identifiers differently (customer-visible naming)?
- Audit log deep links: do we land in global audit log area with pre-filter, or an embedded panel within the Optimize config area?
- Incidents: if rollback triggered from incident-bot deep link, do we auto-fill reason with incident id? (Probably yes, but still editable.)
- Accessibility: destructive action confirmation needs clear focus states and keyboard-safe flows.
- Localization: not in scope now, but avoid idioms.

Appendix: pseudo-wireframes (text)
History tab
[Scope picker: Customer = Acme | Deployment = Dedicated | Region = us-east-1 | Route = /v1/chat | Model = llama-3.1-70b]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
v17   Live    2024-12-03 14:22   Hannah R.   "raise batch tokens"   ENG-4824   Applied to 3 clusters   [Compare] [Rollback]
v16   Applied  2024-12-02 09:10   Felix S.    "enable prefix cache" SUP-2418   Applied to 3 clusters   [Compare] [Rollback]
v15   Known-good 2024-11-28 18:05  Dylan B.    "baseline"           -          Applied to 3 clusters   [Compare] [Rollback]

Rollback modal
Title: Rollback optimization config?
Blast radius: Dedicated / Acme / us-east-1 (3 clusters) / /v1/chat + llama-3.1-70b
Top changes:
- Quantization: int8 → fp16
- Prefix cache: disabled → enabled
Reason: [______________________]
[Cancel] [Rollback]

End notes
This doc is a working scratchpad; as decisions harden, we should migrate stable content to Confluence PRD/design spec and keep this as early exploration + copy drafts.
